judgements.reason: SemisimpleAlgebras is essentially already in Tau Ceti (canonical Wedderburn invariants, double centralizer, Skolem-Noether, the centralizer theorem, the Brauer group with splitting fields and Br(R) = Z/2), leaving only API. GlobalQuadraticForms still needs local and global class field theory (norm index, cyclic Hasse norm theorem, Hilbert reciprocity), Hilbert symbols and the classification of forms over dyadic and non-dyadic local fields, and then Hasse-Minkowski with the existence and classification layers.

GlobalQuadraticForms stacks almost all of class field theory (class formations, local Brauer invariants, the idele-class inequalities, global reciprocity, the norm index, the Hasse norm theorem, Hilbert reciprocity) and local quadratic-form invariants under Hasse-Minkowski and O'Meara's existence theorem. Coleman needs Kubota-Leopoldt L-functions, locally analytic distributions, wide opens with overconvergent de Rham cohomology and Frobenius continuation, and then polylogarithms: a real but shorter p-adic analytic stack.

FunctionFieldArithmetic needs a full class field theory for function fields, the Weil bound through etale duality and abelian schemes, Bruhat-Tits buildings, parahorics and Satake for automorphic forms on G(A_K), and Chebotarev. Coleman's missing theory is limited to p-adic measures and distributions, Kubota-Leopoldt L-functions, wide opens with Frobenius continuation, and polylogarithms.

HigherLocalFields rests on the Voevodsky-Rost norm-residue theorem (transfers and motivic homotopy, motivic Steenrod operations, Rost motives), with Quillen, Waldhausen and scheme K-theory and intersection theory beneath it, followed by higher duality, higher local reciprocity and Kato-Saito global reciprocity. FunctionFieldArithmetic needs function-field class field theory, Weil bounds through etale duality and abelian schemes, and Bruhat-Tits with Satake for automorphic forms: large, but a shallower stack.

Arakelov needs abelian schemes with duals and deformation theory, Neron models and semistable reduction, Siegel/PEL moduli with degenerations and integral toroidal and minimal compactifications, Shimura canonical models and resolution of singularities before the Faltings height and its moduli comparison. HigherLocalFields' decisive cost is the norm-residue theorem, with K-theory and scheme foundations beneath it, plus Kato-Saito higher global reciprocity; this is close, but Arakelov's closure is about twice as large and stacked deeper.

Both are very far. Borel needs higher algebraic K-theory from the plus construction through scheme K-theory with Adams operations and the motivic spectral sequence, Borel-Serre, and Borel's analytic stable-cohomology and regulator/zeta theorems. Arakelov needs the moduli tower (abelian schemes, PEL moduli, Faltings-Chai style compactifications, Shimura canonical models) plus Neron models and resolution of singularities, which is somewhat larger and deeper.

Borel needs the whole of higher algebraic K-theory (plus construction, Q- and S-constructions, K_2 and K_3 with Bloch groups, finite fields, scheme K-theory, the motivic spectral sequence), Borel-Serre, and Borel's stable-cohomology and regulator theorems. LocalGaloisDeformationRings needs rigid geometry, period rings with p-adic local monodromy, Breuil-Kisin modules and deformation functors under Kisin's rings, which is a clearly smaller closure.

Anabelian needs geometric p-adic comparison through A_inf and prismatic cohomology, log-crystalline and Hyodo-Kato theory, perfectoid spaces, diamonds and the relative Fargues-Fontaine curve, together with Poitou-Tate duality, etale fundamental groups and Coleman integration, before reconstruction, Selmer varieties and quadratic Chabauty. LocalGaloisDeformationRings needs only local period rings with monodromy, rigid geometry and Breuil-Kisin modules under Kisin's rings, and Anabelian's closure already contains most of that.

EllipticRegulators' closure contains almost all of Anabelian's prerequisites (p-adic comparison, diamonds, Poitou-Tate duality, Coleman integration). On top of these it needs modularity of elliptic curves over Q with its lifting machinery, the full K-theory and motivic stack including the norm-residue theorem, and Borel and syntomic regulators. Anabelian adds only its own reconstruction and Selmer-variety layers, etale fundamental groups, heights and scheme foundations.

EllipticRegulators' closure already includes the Fargues-Fontaine stages F0-F3 with perfectoid spaces, diamonds and diamond etale cohomology. It adds modular parametrisations and modularity, K_2 of curves with Deligne and syntomic regulators, Borel regulators and the norm-residue theorem. FarguesFontaineDiamonds adds only its Cartier-divisor and derived etale comparison stages.

HodgeTate's closure contains Fargues-Fontaine's untilt, quotient and etale-site comparisons (F0-F3) with perfectoid spaces and diamonds. It adds Shimura varieties with PEL moduli and toroidal compactifications, relative p-adic Hodge theory with A_inf and log-crystalline comparison, canonical subgroups and logarithmic Riemann-Hilbert. FarguesFontaineDiamonds adds only F4-F5, with their diamond etale cohomology, six-operations and classical adic etale inputs.

CompletedCohomology's closure contains nearly all of HodgeTate's foundations (Shimura and PEL moduli, compactifications, p-adic Hodge theory, diamonds). It adds Weil I-II, the trace formula with Jacquet-Langlands and endoscopic transfer, Galois representations of modular and Hilbert forms, integral modular curves, Colmez's p-adic local Langlands with (phi,Gamma)-modules, and Emerton's completed cohomology. HodgeTate adds only canonical subgroups, Igusa towers and log Riemann-Hilbert.

Beyond their shared base (Shimura varieties and compactifications, perfectoid spaces, diamonds, p-adic Hodge theory), PerfectoidShimuraVarieties adds only the Hodge-Tate/canonical-subgroup roadmap and the perfectoid Siegel, Hodge-type and pre-abelian towers. CompletedCohomology adds Weil I-II, the automorphic trace formula and Jacquet-Langlands, Galois representations of modular forms, integral modular curves, p-adic local Langlands for GL_2(Q_p) and completed-cohomology finiteness, about 187 prerequisite layers against 32.

PerfectoidShimuraVarieties uses every layer of HodgeTate (T0-T6: canonical subgroups, Hodge-Tate maps, log Riemann-Hilbert). It also adds infinite-level towers as diamonds, the perfectoid Siegel and Hodge-type constructions with minimal compactifications, Hansen-Johansson pre-abelian descent, general canonical models and general period maps.

CompletedCohomology's closure contains Fargues-Fontaine's perfectoid, diamond, diamond-etale and F0-F3 inputs. It adds modular-curve and Shimura-curve geometry, Weil I-II, the trace formula and Jacquet-Langlands, Galois representations of modular forms, p-adic local Langlands and completed cohomology. FarguesFontaineDiamonds adds only its Cartier-divisor and derived etale comparison stages.

EllipticRegulators' closure already contains HigherLocalFields' K-theory and the whole norm-residue theorem. It adds Borel regulators, modularity of elliptic curves, Deligne and syntomic regulators and p-adic Hodge theory. HigherLocalFields adds only its own higher local and global class field theory layers and scheme foundations.

PerfectoidShimuraVarieties' closure contains nearly all of Arakelov's prerequisites (abelian schemes, PEL moduli, Shimura varieties, toroidal compactifications, resolution). It adds perfectoid spaces, diamonds, A_inf and crystalline p-adic Hodge theory, the whole Hodge-Tate/canonical-subgroup roadmap and the perfectoid towers. Arakelov adds only Neron models with semistable reduction and its six height layers.

Anabelian uses Coleman's Frobenius continuation (L0-L1). It adds geometric p-adic comparison via A_inf and prismatic cohomology and diamonds, Poitou-Tate duality, etale fundamental groups, anabelian reconstruction, Selmer varieties and quadratic Chabauty. Coleman adds only polylogarithms and Theorem 6.7, Kubota-Leopoldt L-functions, and the growth and Mellin-transform layers of locally analytic distributions.

FunctionFieldArithmetic spreads over three towers: etale duality and abelian schemes for the Weil bound; Bruhat-Tits buildings with Satake (over reductive structure theory) for automorphic forms on G(A_K); and a full function-field class field theory with Chebotarev. LocalGaloisDeformationRings is one taller tower of rigid geometry, period rings with p-adic local monodromy and Breuil-Kisin modules under Kisin's deformation rings. The two are close in size, with FunctionFieldArithmetic slightly larger.

Borel needs algebraic K-theory from the plus construction up, Borel-Serre with Borel's stable cohomology, regulators with Dedekind zeta leading terms, and the motivic spectral sequence. GlobalQuadraticForms needs class field theory and local quadratic-form invariants under Hasse-Minkowski, on a baseline that already has Witt theory, weak approximation and localized forms.

HodgeTate needs Shimura varieties with PEL moduli and compactifications, perfectoid spaces and diamonds, relative p-adic Hodge theory and log Riemann-Hilbert before canonical subgroups and Hodge-Tate period maps. Coleman needs only p-adic measures and distributions, Kubota-Leopoldt L-functions, wide opens with Frobenius continuation, and polylogarithms.

HigherLocalFields rests on the Voevodsky-Rost norm-residue theorem (motivic homotopy, Steenrod operations, Rost motives) with Quillen and scheme K-theory beneath it, followed by Kato duality, higher local reciprocity and Kato-Saito global reciprocity. LocalGaloisDeformationRings needs rigid geometry, period rings with p-adic local monodromy and Breuil-Kisin modules before Kisin's rings, which is a smaller stack.

EllipticRegulators' closure contains FunctionFieldArithmetic's etale duality, Weil bounds, abelian schemes, Bruhat-Tits and Satake inputs. It adds modularity of elliptic curves, the norm-residue and motivic K-theory stack, and Borel and syntomic regulators. FunctionFieldArithmetic adds only its own function-field class field theory, Chebotarev and automorphic layers plus scheme foundations.

Arakelov needs abelian schemes, Neron models and semistable reduction, PEL moduli with Faltings-Chai style compactifications and Shimura canonical models before Faltings heights can be compared. GlobalQuadraticForms needs class field theory and local quadratic-form invariants under Hasse-Minkowski, on a baseline that already covers its localizations and Witt theory.
